subject.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks

question: Should file-based internal hooks gain an observation-only outbound `message:sending` event despite current documentation reserving rewrite and cancellation policy for typed plugin hooks?
rationale: The internal registry cannot honor the documented modifying-hook contract, so choosing its permanent semantics and name is a product and security-boundary decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Keep policy plugin-only
options.body: Reject the parallel internal event and continue directing filtering, rewriting, and cancellation to typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Add an observer event
options.body: Approve a documented observation-only event that runs after typed policy hooks and never fires for canceled delivery.

options.title: Redesign internal hooks
options.body: Pause this PR and design awaited, ordered, explicitly modifying internal-hook semantics as a broader compatibility project.

recommendation.title: Keep policy plugin-only
recommendation.body: Reject the parallel internal event and continue directing filtering, rewriting, and cancellation to typed plugin hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: Their current exactly-once delivery work spans the shared dispatcher and channel-specific hook ownership boundary affected by this choice.
